title: Maestro di color che sanno
html_source:
From Dante’s Inferno (4:131), meaning “master of those that know.”

This is Dante’s name for Aristotle.

The juxtaposition, too, of the Italian ‘color’ and the English ‘colour’, a connection Joyce thoroughly intended.

anchor.prefix: diaphane. But he adds: in bodies. Then he was aware of them bodies before of them coloured. How? By knocking his sconce against them, sure. Go easy. Bald he was and a millionaire,
anchor.suffix:
. Limit of the diaphane in. Why in? Diaphane, adiaphane. If you can put your five fingers through it it is a gate, if not a door. Shut your eyes and see. 

 Stephen closed his eyes
